meaning: The number of descendants of Besai (Neh 7:23); mathematically 18 × 18, without any well-established symbolic meaning
description: The number 324 appears in the Bible in Nehemiah 7:23, where it is given as the count of descendants of Besai who returned from exile in Babylon. Such census figures in Ezra-Nehemiah primarily serve as historical documentation of those who returned to Judah after the Babylonian captivity. Beyond this specific occurrence, 324 has no well-established symbolic meaning in classical biblical or Jewish tradition. Although gematria may link the number to certain Hebrew words, there is no broad scholarly consensus on a specific symbolic interpretation.

versions.meaning: The number 324 has no well-established or prominent symbolic significance in biblical or Jewish tradition.
versions.description: 324 is not a number that appears with special significance in the Bible or in well-known Jewish numerological (gematria) traditions. Although gematria can link the number to certain Hebrew words or expressions, there is no broad consensus among scholars regarding a specific symbolic meaning for this number. Some may point out that 324 is 18 × 18 (where 18 represents 'chai', life), which in popular Jewish tradition could be interpreted as an intensified blessing of life, but this is not a classical or authoritative interpretation.

footnotes.text: 324 is 18 × 18. Since 18 is the numerical value of the Hebrew word חי (chai, 'life'), in popular Jewish tradition 324 can be interpreted as an intensified blessing of life—"life times life." However, this is not a classical or authoritative interpretation.

In the parallel list in Ezra 2:17, the descendants of Besai are given as 323, that is, one fewer than in Nehemiah 7:23. Such minor discrepancies between lists are common and may be due to different times of counting or scribal errors.
